slices.label: Women outside the South

slices.label: White Southerners
slices.source: 1930–1940 interpolation to November 1932, white adults (including Mexican-origin adults, listed separately in 1930) in the eleven former Confederate states; poll taxes in most of them; calibrated to certified 1932 returns.

slices.label: Black Southerners
slices.source: 1930–1940 interpolation to November 1932, Black adults in the eleven former Confederate states; disfranchisement by poll tax, literacy test and the white primary continues, so the shortfall against white turnout is counted as exclusion.

slices.label: Immigrants not yet citizens
slices.source: 1930–1940 interpolation to November 1932, foreign-born white adults who were not naturalized; no state let aliens vote after 1926.

runs.summary: Rerun with nothing changed, 1932 comes out as it did: Roosevelt wins, 472–59. The closest state was Connecticut, which went to Hoover by 1.1 points. Every one of my 100 reruns reproduces it exactly.
howIGotThis: The numbers: the 1930 and 1940 census counts interpolated to 1932 and certified returns; every draw reproduces 1932 exactly before the change.
How sure: I reran it 100 times with different population and parameter draws.

south-white.name: Anna Reed
south-white.quote: Things are desperate for so many people we know. The fellow from New York says the government ought to actually help, not just wait around hoping business picks up.
south-white.controlQuote: Things are desperate for so many people we know. The fellow from New York says the government ought to actually help, not just wait around hoping business picks up.

women.name: Ruth Robinson
women.quote: The Democrat talks about helping us farmers actually get our costs back. The President's been in four years and things just got worse for us.
women.controlQuote: The Democrat talks about helping us farmers actually get our costs back. The President's been in four years and things just got worse for us.

men.name: Ernest Reed
men.quote: The other fellow says the government ought to help us with real money for work and relief. That's what we need right now, not promises about banks getting better.
